comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount (not premium) rests on evidence that persists through the horizon: (1) structurally lower margins - ST GM 34.8% in Q2-26 (src 3) vs TXN 61% (src 9), NXP 57-58% (src 10), MCHP 63.8% (src 12) and IFX 40.8% (src 11); target only >40% after reshaping ends ~end-2027 (src 4); (2) higher cyclicality - op. margin went 26.7% (2023) -> 1.5% (2025) (F5/F1, F7/F3), and P&D still lost $99M in Q2-26 (src 13); (3) the horizon NTM EPS will sit ~1.75 years into a price-led upcycle with book-to-bill ~2 and extending lead times (src 4, 14), where the market typically pays below-median multiples. No sell-side outperformance claim is used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$34 (~31% under today's $49.57) the market would be pricing NTM EPS well under $2 at a ~17x multiple - i.e. the 2027 recovery (consensus FY2027 EPS $2.69) failing: bookings/backlog unwinding (double-ordering), gross margin stuck in the mid-30s after reshaping, or data-center/LEO programmes slipping. That is a fundamental miss, not ordinary 61%-vol noise around a $50 centre.

reverse_dcf_check: model_engine: at the stated cash flows (FY2029 GAAP EBIT margin 17%, 3% terminal growth) the 17.5x P/E / 9.5x EV/EBITDA multiples imply a WACC of 8.8% versus the 10.9% built from a 5.21% 10-year Treasury (src 42) and beta 1.48 (src 7); equivalently, at 10.9% the multiples need terminal margins/growth above my base. That is why the DCF leg ($41) sits below the multiple legs ($51-59) and why I hold the P/E below the 21.5x peer median; the multiples remain plausible only if ST holds mid/high-teens margins through the 2028 cycle risk, which the reshaping (>40% GM target, src 4) supports but does not guarantee.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT (after SBC, 1.4% of revenue) used throughout; shares fall only 0.5%/yr net of share-award deliveries; peer forward P/Es are non-GAAP (mostly SBC-inclusive for analog IDMs), so the 17.5x is applied to GAAP EPS which is slightly below non-GAAP (reshaping costs) - a mild conservative bias.

reasoning: Facts: $49.57, 52-week $21.11-81.42; FY2025 revenue $11.8B, GAAP EBIT $175M (F3,F7); H1-26 revenue +24.6% (src 2); Q2-26 $3.49B, GM 34.8%, book-to-bill ~2, backlog 4.5-5 quarters, Q3 guide $3.70B/37%, Q4 >$4B, ~$18B revenue in 2028 target (src 3,4). The stock peaked in June and fell ~40% as Q2 margins/EBITDA and the Q3 guide missed (src 5) and, in October, on sector-wide AI-revenue doubts (src 18). Industry lane: the whole analog/power chain is in a price-led upcycle - TXN Q2 +23% with price increases from Q3 (src 9), NXP +19% with Q3 +15-21% (src 10), Microchip +38%, distributor inventory 25 days, broad price hike (src 12), Infineon record quarter and +13% q/q guide but auto slower (src 11), twelve price-increase notices incl. two from ST (src 14), WSTS/SIA totals +100%+ but memory-led (src 16,17), China LV production cut for 2027 (src 15), SiC price war bottoming (src 13). So 2027 earnings recovery (consensus EPS $2.69, src 6) looks well supported, but ST's margins lag every peer and the cycle will be ~1.75 years old at the horizon. Valuation: engine base $50.3 (DCF 41 / P/E 51 / EV/EBITDA 59); scenarios $25.7/50.3/73.2 at 25/50/25%. Ladder is a lognormal mixture around those scenario values (vol ~24-32% within scenario), giving median ~$50, P(>=$74) ~16% and P(<=$30) ~16% - narrower than a pure 61%-vol lognormal because valuation anchors the centre, but with a fat left tail for a cycle turn. Research limited: Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage premium estimate endpoints were not used as sources (key/plan gated); several press pages (ST IR, GlobeNewswire copies, Nasdaq) returned 403/503; sec.gov refused curl so filings were read via WebFetch.
